key_insight: Supersonic atmospheric plasma spraying at an optimal 100 mm stand-off produces intact ZrC splats and promotes strong inter-splat bonding through zirconia phase evolution, columnar interfacial grains, and an amorphous Zr-Si-O adhesion layer.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies microstructural features that can be tuned to improve cohesion, adhesion, and high-temperature durability in ceramic thermal-spray coatings.
method: Prepared ZrC splats by high-temperature atmospheric plasma spraying at varied spraying distances.
Characterized splat morphology, phase composition, and cross-sectional interface structure.
Compared stacked splat evolution and splat-substrate interfacial features.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that 100 mm was optimal for disk-shaped, non-splashed splats and documents phase/interface observations including t-ZrO2, m-ZrO2, ~150 nm columnar grains, and an amorphous Zr-Si-O interlayer.
watch_item: The findings are highly dependent on spraying distance and process conditions, so the interface structure may not transfer directly to other plasma-spray setups or substrates.
paper_title: Microstructure and interface characteristics of ZrC splats prepared by high temperature atmospheric plasma deposition
